about: Camera notch housings of MacBook panels, in panel pixels, for NotchModel.js. Omarchy's display-cutouts.json says which screens have a notch and how tall it is; it has no width or shape. notchWidth is the housing along the screen's top edge; radius is its bottom corners; shoulder is the inside curve where the top edge turns down into it. A panel is matched by its physical mode, as there. Widths come from macOS readings (NSScreen auxiliaryTopLeftArea/RightArea) taken at a scaled mode, converted: points x native width / scaled width. 'measured' rows convert a reading on that panel; 'inferred' rows assume the same camera housing as a measured panel of the same pixel density. Corners: roughly 4 pt shoulders and 8 pt bottom corners at the 14-inch Pro's 2x (https://notchbay.com/blog/macbook-notch-size/), the same at the 16-inch's equal density; the Airs' scaled by density (224/254), not measured.

panels.source: 220 x 38 pt at 2056 x 1329 on Mac16,7 (AppKit): https://crestnotch.app/macbook-notch-dimensions
209 x 38 pt at 1710 x 1112 on Mac14,2 (auxiliary areas 751 + 750): https://github.com/valenvivaldi/notch-fight/pull/1
No reading found; the 13.6-inch Air's housing at the same 224 ppi.
